name: Currency | Add currency accepts a code that is not ISO 4217 and silently rounds the exchange rate
description_html:
Summary

The add-currency API accepts a currency code that isn't a real ISO 4217 code, and it rounds an exchange rate with too many decimals without telling the user. Both were found through the API (POST /api/v1/currencies); the screen uses a currency picker.

Environment

  • TAVI CRM: staging-crm.taviportal.com, tenant NDC-Staging, account ndc-staging-owner
  • Zoho CRM (reference): test org, checked live in Edge
  • Date: 17 Nov 2026

Steps to reproduce

  1. Add a currency with code XYZ, symbol x, rate 2.
  2. Add EUR with rate 0.123456789012 (12 decimal places).

Expected result

  • XYZ is refused. The error text for bad codes already says "Currency code must be a 3-letter ISO 4217 code".
  • A rate with too many decimals is refused with a message. Zoho CRM shows "Exchange rate is too large" and keeps Save disabled.

Actual result

  • XYZ is created (201) and listed as "XYZ · XYZ".
  • The rate is saved as 0.123456789 without any message.

Already correct

Rate 0, negative or over 1,000,000,000, a blank symbol, a symbol over 8 characters, the home currency and duplicate codes are all refused with clear errors.
